text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Around 56.8 percent of Poland's voters voted in favour of the constitution produced by the parliamentary majority while 43.2 percent were against, an exit poll conducted by the PBS polling agency during a referendum on Sunday said.
- Although EU markets are becoming more open to Polish-made goods exporters will have to compete hard to sell them, EU officials said.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Poland's national flag carrier PLL LOT should start co-operation with one of Europe's five biggest airlines as the benefits would outweigh disadvantages, the Dutch KLM's president Pieter Bouw said.

- Poland's treasury ministry has shortlisted three investors interested in buying an 80 percent stake in the ZR Romet bicycle maker in Bydgoszcz now under privatisation. The listed Universal foreign trade company is one contender but no other facts were disclosed, Romet's spokesperson Malgorzata Pelc said.
- Poland's computer hardware and software market is now worth around $1.0 billion a year and will grow to $6.0 billion by 2000, the Unisys computer firm's president Krzysztof Korba said.

- The Huta Szkla Warta glassworks in Sierakow Wielkopolski, western Poland, has installed a computerised bottle production line, which increased the plant's output capacity by 70 percent, and obtained the International Standards Organisation (ISO)-9001 quality system certificate, the company said.

- The Ponar-Wadowice power hydraulics equipment maker is planning a C-series share issue of 67,000 shares priced at 3.47 zlotys per share in December this year. The issue, to be listed on the Warsaw bourse's parallel market, will be addressed to individual investors, the company said.

- The ZM Kolo meat processing plant will present a share issue prospectus to the Polish Securities Commission (KPW) by the end of June and apply for a bourse listing in the fourth quarter of 1997, the company said. ZM Kolo wants to sell 3.2 million A, B, C, and D-series shares priced at 10 zlotys per share, the plant's president Jerzy Marciniak said.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI
- The state-owned Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej (BGZ) agricultural sector bank will issue bonds in three tranches of $30 million each in the second half of the year, the bank said.

- The Budbank construction development bank's net profit was 30 percent higher in the first quarter of 1997 than in the same period last year, the bank's president Jerzy Radko said. Budbank's balance sheet total grew by 60 percent and deposits soared by 200 percent, Radko said.
- The listed Animex food processing group will invest 200 million zlotys in development by 2000, the company's board said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- Poland's treasury ministry has published a list of 20 firms to be assisted by the World Bank on their way to the regulated Over-the-Counter-Market (OTC).
- Financial institutions spent 105 million zlotys on advertising campaigns in 1996, a survey by the Optimedia Poland polling agency said.
ZYCIE
- The listed Bank Inicjatyw Gospodarczych and Bank Gdanski will merge into one, the banks' boards decided on Friday.
NOTE - Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
